The ticket may be written to the driver, the carrier, or both; who is named changes who has to answer and what the defense looks like.

sections.heading: Where Trucking Tickets Come From in El Paso County
paragraphs: Two fixed inspection stations bracket El Paso on Interstate 10: the DPS commercial vehicle inspection facility at Anthony, just inside the Texas line on the west side, and the Hudspeth County station east of the county past Fort Hancock. Between them, DPS commercial vehicle enforcement troopers work the interstate, Loop 375 and the Border Highway, and El Paso Police and the Sheriff pull trucks in the industrial corridors along Zaragoza Road and Joe Battle Boulevard.

A roadside inspection can end three ways: a clean report, violations noted with no citation, or violations plus one or more citations. The citation is a Class C misdemeanor filed in the Justice of the Peace precinct where the stop happened, or in Anthony or Vinton municipal court if a city officer wrote it. Our flat fee in those courts is $69 per citation, with additional citations from the same inspection as discounted add-ons.

Drayage drivers from Juárez, owner-operators based in Horizon City and Socorro, and over-the-road drivers only passing through all end up in the same courts. We generally resolve the ticket without the driver coming back to El Paso.

sections.heading: Driver vs. Carrier: Who Gets the Ticket and Who Has to Answer
paragraphs: Inspectors decide at the roadside whether a violation belongs to the driver, the motor carrier, or both. A logbook violation is generally the driver's. A brake adjustment or missing annual inspection is usually written to the carrier, though the driver can be cited for operating the vehicle with the defect. Overweight tickets commonly name the driver and list the carrier. Who is named determines who is the defendant in JP court, whose record the conviction goes on, and who signs the engagement with our office.

This matters because a driver's and a carrier's interests are not the same in every case. An owner-operator with his own authority is both; a company driver may be told by dispatch that "the company handles it" when the company is only handling its own citation. We ask for every citation from the inspection, confirm who is named on each, and protect the driver's personal record even when the carrier is paying for the defense. A driver's conviction is reported to DPS and appears on the motor vehicle record every future employer pulls.

sections.heading: A JP Court Ticket Is Not an FMCSA Civil Penalty — or a CSA Score
paragraphs: Drivers and carriers often confuse three separate things. The citation is a Texas criminal charge — a Class C misdemeanor — heard in a JP or municipal court and resolved by dismissal, plea or trial. That is what our office handles. An FMCSA civil penalty is a federal administrative fine, usually issued to a carrier after a compliance review, and contested through the agency, not a Texas court. The CSA score (Compliance, Safety, Accountability) is the carrier's safety rating built from roadside inspection data, updated whether or not a citation is ever filed.

Winning the ticket helps, but it does not automatically clean the inspection report. Carriers who want the violation removed from their CSA profile file a DataQs challenge with FMCSA, and a court dismissal is useful supporting evidence. When we resolve a trucking citation, we provide the signed dismissal order so the carrier's safety department can use it.

Because CDL holders are generally excluded from the deferred disposition and defensive driving programs that resolve so many El Paso tickets, we focus on the facts: scale certification, the wording of the report, whether the cited regulation actually applies to the vehicle and load, and whether the defect was corrected. Many trucking citations are resolved on proof of repair or proof that a permit covered the movement. See how ticket dismissals work in El Paso courts.

sections.heading: Out-of-Service Orders: Fix It, Document It, Keep Every Page
paragraphs: An out-of-service order means the driver or the vehicle can't move until the problem is fixed — a driver past hours, brakes below standard, an unsecured load. Violating one carries its own CDL disqualification consequences under federal rules, so never drive off the Anthony lot because dispatch said to. Fix the problem, document the repair with a dated invoice, and keep every piece of paper from the stop.

Then send us the citations through the online hire form or call 915-503-1600 before the appearance date on each one. We file a notice of appearance in the right JP precinct promptly, which prevents a failure-to-appear charge and a warrant while you are two states away. If a date was already missed, our warrant recall page explains how we ask the court to lift it. Se habla español, and we work with Mexican carriers and drivers crossing at Zaragoza every week. This page is general information, not legal advice about your case.

faqs.q: Which court handles a ticket from the Anthony inspection station?
faqs.a: DPS citations from the Anthony scales or I-10 are filed in the El Paso County Justice of the Peace precinct covering that area, or in Anthony or Vinton municipal court if a city officer wrote them. Hudspeth County station tickets are filed in Hudspeth County. Our flat fee for El Paso County JP and area city courts is $69 per citation.

faqs.q: Can I use deferred disposition or defensive driving on a trucking ticket?
faqs.a: Generally not if you hold a CDL. Texas excludes CDL holders from the driving safety course dismissal, and federal anti-masking rules generally bar deferrals for commercial drivers. We work for an outright dismissal or a reduction to a non-reportable charge instead.

faqs.q: The ticket is in the company's name. Do I still need a lawyer?
faqs.a: Check every citation from the inspection. Carrier-named tickets go on the carrier's record; driver-named tickets go on yours. If any citation names you, your personal record is at stake regardless of what the company does with its own tickets, and we represent you.

faqs.q: If the ticket is dismissed, does the violation come off my CSA score?
faqs.a: Not automatically. CSA data comes from the inspection report, not the court. The carrier files a DataQs challenge with FMCSA, and a court dismissal is useful evidence in that challenge. We provide the dismissal order for that purpose.

faqs.q: What happens if I just pay an overweight ticket?
faqs.a: Paying is a guilty plea. The fine on a heavy overweight ticket can be substantial, and the conviction is reported to DPS for employers to see. Overweight citations are among the more negotiable we handle, so paying without reviewing the weight ticket and permit often costs more than it saves.

faqs.q: I'm an over-the-road driver. Do I have to come back to El Paso for court?
faqs.a: Generally not. We appear in the JP or municipal court for you and handle the pretrial docket. You would only need to be present for a trial, which is uncommon and something we would schedule around your routes.
